title: Pro-etale direct image commutes with uniformly bounded-below coproducts
statement:
Let $h:T\to U$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], meaning that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact and the diagonal is quasi-compact. Use the small pro-etale sites and universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R_U$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebras on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, set $R_T=h^{-1}R_U$, and use the module sheaves and ordinary uncompleted derived operations [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every small set $I$, integer $N$, and family $K_i\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$ with $H^n(K_i)=0$ for all $n<N$ and $i\in I$, the canonical map induced by the coproduct inclusions is an isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}Rh_*K_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i\right).$$
Here coproducts are the sheafified termwise direct sums of complexes in the indicated derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful].

source.place: Tag 09A3, label lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-commutes-direct-sums; relative Q-algebra module version obtained by forgetting module structure and testing on affine pro-etale objects

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ on the chosen small site. It is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose injective representatives $E_i^\bullet$ of $K_i$, all zero below the given integer $N$. Put $S^\bullet=\bigoplus_iE_i^\bullet$, the sheafified termwise sum stipulated in the item. Sums are exact: a sum is the filtered colimit of finite sums and filtered colimits are exact by the Grothendieck theorem. Thus $H^q(S)=\bigoplus_iH^q(E_i)$, and $S$ is zero below $N$. Choose an injective representative $J^\bullet$ of $QS$ also zero below $N$. The isomorphism $QS\simeq QJ$ is represented by a chain map $a:S\to J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; it is a quasi-isomorphism. Write $a_i:E_i\to J$ for its composites with the inclusions.

source.place: Tag 09A3 proof: common lower bound, representatives and termwise direct sum

proof.text: It suffices to check cohomology presheaves on objects $V\to U$ with $V$ affine and whose map factors through an affine open $A\subset U$: cover any site object by its affine open pieces inside the inverse images of affine opens of $U$. These are still site objects by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The scheme $T_A=h^{-1}(A)$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Choose a finite affine cover $T_A=\bigcup B_j$ with each intersection $B_j\cap B_k$ quasi-compact, because this intersection is the inverse image of the affine $B_j\times_A B_k$ under the quasi-compact diagonal, using the quasi-separated convention [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then $T_V=T_A\times_A V$ has the finite affine cover $B_j\times_A V$. Each pairwise intersection is $(B_j\cap B_k)\times_A V$ and has a finite affine cover obtained by pulling back a finite affine cover of $B_j\cap B_k$. Consequently $T_V$ is qcqs. This explicitly checks the needed base-change property over affine $A$ and affine $V$; no qcqs assertion is made for arbitrary non-quasi-compact site objects.

source.place: Tag 09A3 proof: qcqs object to which the hypercover construction applies

proof.text: For each such $V$, $T_V$ is an object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (weakly etale maps are preserved by this fibre product, as in the base-change site functor of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover] in that site to choose $U_\bullet\to T_V$ with each $U_p$ affine and weakly contractible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-computes-bounded-complex] to $E_i$, $S$, and $J$. It gives natural total-complex models for their derived sections over the object $T_V$. Since $E_i$ and $J$ are injective complexes, the corresponding derived sections are $E_i(T_V)$ and $J(T_V)$.

For an affine $W=U_p$ and any family of module sheaves $F_i$, the map $\bigoplus_iF_i(W)\to(\bigoplus_iF_i)(W)$ is bijective. Indeed [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] constructs module sheafification on the underlying abelian presheaf; [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies its underlying set sheafification. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], every section is therefore locally a finite-support tuple. The covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] gives a finite affine refinement of this cover over the affine $W$; the union of its finitely many finite supports is one finite set $I_0$. Every component outside $I_0$ vanishes locally and hence globally by sheaf separation. Projection to the finite sum on $I_0$ recovers the section, because the projection followed by inclusion agrees with it on this cover. A finite sum of module sheaves is also a finite product, so its sections are the finite sum of the sections of the summands [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Injectivity follows by applying each component projection. These maps commute with restrictions and sheaf morphisms because each is the map induced by the same coproduct inclusions. This supplies the module case of Tag 0935 directly; it does not assume evaluation is exact.

source.place: Tag 09A3 proof: sites-modules.tex Tag 0935, label lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact, clause (2), finite-support argument

proof.text: Apply step 4 to $F_i=E_i^q$ on every $U_p$. In total degree $r$ the only possible indices are $0\leq p\leq r-N$, so exchanging this finite sum with the sum over $i$ gives $$\operatorname{Tot}(S(U_\bullet))^r=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Tot}(E_i(U_\bullet))^r.$$ On the summand $E_i^q(U_p)$ both differentials are the same alternating restrictions plus $(-1)^p d_{E_i}$; thus these degreewise maps give an isomorphism of complexes compatible with every inclusion. Step 3 identifies its derived image with the canonical map $\bigoplus_iR\Gamma(T_V,K_i)\to R\Gamma(T_V,QS)$. Composing with the map induced by $a$ gives the map $\bigoplus_iE_i(T_V)\to J(T_V)$, which is a quasi-isomorphism. The sum of the complexes of sections represents their derived coproduct by [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums].

source.place: Tag 09A3 proof: finite diagonals in the common bounded-below total complexes

proof.text: Set $P^\bullet=\bigoplus_i(h_*E_i^\bullet)$, initially as a complex of presheaves of $R_U$-modules, and let $b:P\to h_*J$ be induced by $h_*a_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $P(V)=\bigoplus_iE_i(T_V)$ and $(h_*J)(V)=J(T_V)$, so step 5 says $b(V)$ is a quasi-isomorphism on every affine object of the basis in step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], $H^q(P^\#)\simeq H^q(P)^\#$, and the cohomology sheaf of $h_*J$ is the sheafification of its cohomology presheaf. Therefore $H^q(b^\#)$ is the sheafification of a presheaf map that is an isomorphism on that basis. Its kernel and cokernel presheaves vanish there. Any map from either presheaf into a sheaf is zero: restrict a section to the covering by basis objects and use sheaf separation. The sheafification adjunction then makes their sheafifications zero. Exact sheafification consequently makes $H^q(b^\#)$ an isomorphism for every $q$.

source.place: Relative version of Tag 09A3; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0BKV, label lemma-sheafification-cohomology, explicit kernel/image calculation

proof.text: The complex $P^\#$ is the sheafified termwise sum of $h_*E_i$, hence represents $\bigoplus_iRh_*K_i$ by the coproduct convention in the item and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The complex $h_*J$ represents $Rh_*(\bigoplus_iK_i)$. The morphism $Q(b^\#)$ has the required composites with every coproduct inclusion, namely $Rh_*(K_i\to\bigoplus_iK_i)$; it is therefore the canonical comparison. Both complexes vanish below $N$. Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] show this map is an isomorphism. The bounded-below category is full in the unbounded derived category [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so this is the requested ordinary uncompleted derived isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Replaced the relabelled absolute coproduct theorem by two strictly smaller inputs: affine weakly contractible hypercover existence and the natural total-complex model for one bounded-below module complex. Proved sections of sums by finite support, exchanged the finite diagonals explicitly, and detected the actual comparison on cohomology sheaves over an affine basis.
